records.locator: Chapter II vv114–116, physical PDF p75
records.source_paraphrase: Different lord of Lagna/D9-lord situations are associated with comforts/prosperity beginning after age 16, 20 or 30.
records.limits: Three competing scenarios, not a universal exact onset age; socioeconomic opportunity and imprecise historical timelines require independent data.

records.locator: Chapter III v1, PDF p76
records.source_paraphrase: Original translated source defines second house as dependents, face/mouth/speech, right eye, accumulated wealth, education, eating, servants and friends.
records.limits: Domain inventory, not evidence all domains are predicted with useful specificity; high-stakes conditions excluded.

records.locator: Chapter III v1 Translator's Note, PDF p76
records.source_paraphrase: Bhasin states his own preference for assigning formal education to second house rather than fourth/fifth, treating the latter as desire and intelligence.
records.limits: Do NOT attribute this exclusive school choice to Venkatesha's verse; parent source only lists education among second-house topics.

records.locator: Chapter III vv20–24, PDF p80
records.source_paraphrase: Differing dignity/division/benefic conditions of second-house lord are linked to subsistence hardship, support for twenty dependents, administrative responsibility over 300 or 1,000 people, or protecting very many.
records.limits: Precise number of dependents vs administrative authority are different targets; never treat a large institution title as verified number of dependents.

records.locator: Chapter IV vv54–56, PDF p115
records.source_paraphrase: Fourth-house/ascendant lord conditions allegedly predict acquiring a house, with benefic dignity altering ease of acquisition.
records.limits: Observable property ownership and whether assisted acquisition must be defined, dated and conditioned on financial opportunity.

records.locator: Chapter V opening v1 and Translator's Note, PDF p137
records.source_paraphrase: Verse names intelligence, discrimination and mantra along with children and other affairs as fifth-house domains; Bhasin's subsequent paragraph adds a modern anatomical interpretation of heart/belly/lung rulership.
records.limits: No objective modern neuroscience/medical inference is warranted; distinguish spiritual practice/knowledge from anatomy and commentary.

records.locator: Chapter V, sixth-house vv49–52, PDF p159
records.source_paraphrase: The text describes weakening hostile sixth-house lord with benefic associations and a strong ascendant lord as an indicator of friendship even among enemies; neighboring claims concern broader community cordiality.
records.limits: A historical relational transition, not merely generic kindness; requires independently documented preexisting conflict and reconciliation.

records.locator: Chapter VIII eleventh-house vv2–10, PDF pp212–213
records.source_paraphrase: Eleventh-house lord/occupant conditions predict increased or reduced income, and the predicted direction of income is connected to the sign or strongest planet influencing that house.
records.limits: Separate direction/geography of income from net worth or business success; loss clauses need to be scored, not discarded.

records.locator: Chapter VIII twelfth-house vv1–7, PDF pp214–215
records.source_paraphrase: The text maps twelfth house to expenses, sleep and losses and gives different formulas for morally categorized legitimate versus illegitimate spending.
records.limits: Historical moral labels must never be applied as personal factual judgments; actual spending categories require contemporary neutral definitions.

records.locator: Chapter XV Venus major period vv25–30, PDF p320
records.source_paraphrase: A Venus-period series differentiates welfare work, material gains/losses, charity and becoming known through writing according to natal Venus house and condition.
records.limits: Prospective timing window and endpoints must be declared; claims that both gain and loss occur are intrinsically weakly specific.

records.locator: Chapter XVI p366 Translator's Note after subperiod discussion
records.source_paraphrase: Bhasin supplies a known relationship-separation case to illustrate Rahu/Ketu/Sun impacts during major/subperiods.
records.limits: Known marriage outcome is developmental illustration only, NOT blinded historical predictive confirmation.

records.locator: Adhyaya XI slokas81–85, PDF pp750–751 / printed740–741
records.source_paraphrase: Translated Vaidyanatha verses identify separate combinations for mathematicians, argumentation specialists, grammarians and students of ontology.
records.limits: These specialized educational tracks are not equivalent to generic intelligence; exact strength and varga requirements differ and must be frozen.

records.locator: Adhyaya XI sloka86, PDF p751 / printed741
records.source_paraphrase: Jupiter in angle and specific Venus/Mercury divisional strengths are said to produce proficiency in six traditional sciences.
records.limits: Need a declared historical-to-modern course taxonomy and exact D9/varga feature; cannot score any scientific interest as success.

records.locator: Adhyaya XI sloka88, PDF p751 / printed741
records.source_paraphrase: Sastri explicitly reports that latter half of sloka 88 is missing in all manuscripts available to him.
records.limits: Do not invent completion from combinatorial plausibility or borrow another source silently; further manuscript evidence needed.

records.locator: Adhyaya XI slokas55–56, PDF p741 / printed731
records.source_paraphrase: The original translated rules distinguish financial gain through a brother versus inheritance/property from mother based on second-house lord and associated third/fourth lord.
records.limits: Historical family financial events have independent record quality and may overlap earlier Saravali/Parashara rules; not validation.

records.locator: Adhyaya XVII slokas14–16, PDF p985 / printed976
records.source_paraphrase: A Kalachakra-Dasha rule classifies positive effects when Mercury/Jupiter/Venus occupy the Deha/Jiva sign and mixed effects when malefics and benefics share it.
records.limits: Source includes a distinct 'Parasara adds' note; record as transmitted textual layers and do not conflate author/speaker.

records.locator: Adhyaya XVIII sloka6, PDF p1017 / printed1007
records.source_paraphrase: A period's favorable outcome is connected to the rising sign at the time the daśā begins, its lord and saptavarga relation.
records.limits: Time of period commencement is a separate chart datum requiring original sunrise, calendar, location and ephemeris calculations; not just natal chart.

records.locator: Adhyaya XVIII editor note after sloka6, PDF p1017
records.source_paraphrase: The Sastri NOTES explicitly says the next five slokas are taken from Śrīpati Paddhati.
records.limits: A received book may contain borrowed lines; preserve dependence instead of counting as independent Vaidyanatha confirmation.

records.locator: Adhyaya XVIII slokas22–23, PDF p1025 / printed1015
records.source_paraphrase: Verse22 separates worship of a planet's deity, attainment in religious austerity during ninth-house-lord daśā, and rites during tenth-house-lord period; verse23 adds predominant sattva/rajas/tamas and nakshatra group conditions.
records.limits: Ninth and tenth source words verified from rendered page. Voluntary practice and metaphysical claims must be kept distinct; not observable astrology success.

records.locator: Lesson9, PDF pp190–204, especially p190
records.source_paraphrase: Sanjay Rath derives Sanskrit name-letter numerical positions by phonetic varga groups and matras, using transliteration and individual phoneme counts.
records.limits: This requires a name, pronunciation/language and explicit transliteration convention beyond birth data; not literal Jaimini sutra prediction.

records.locator: Lesson13 Sutra1.1.2 + commentary, PDF pp257–258
records.source_paraphrase: The book treats sign-to-sign aspects as a permanent relationship: movable to nonadjacent fixed, fixed to nonadjacent movable, and dual to other dual signs.
records.limits: Do not substitute Graha-Drsti planetary aspects; comments about facing architecture and certain regional chart layouts are Rath's explanation, not sky physics.

records.locator: Lesson14 Sutra1.1.25 and examples, PDF pp271–273
records.source_paraphrase: Rath uses zodiacal/anti-zodiacal counting from a candidate starting sign by odd/even orientation, with explicit inclusive counting and alternatives from sign or lord.
records.limits: Freeze exact starting sign, sign-lord (dual-lord) resolution and counting direction; cannot select best timing after outcomes.

records.locator: Lesson14 ParaSara Exceptions, PDF pp274–280
records.source_paraphrase: Rath explicitly says his Dasha explanation adopts exceptions from a Parāśara tradition, and asserts disciplinary lineage as rationale for assuming Jaimini and Parāśara rules agree.
records.limits: Religious-lineage assertion is not proof identical original text or mathematically unique algorithm; label adopted exceptions.

records.locator: Lesson14 PDF p282, nonhuman life examples
records.source_paraphrase: Rath assigns a twelve-year maximum sign-daśā period for humans/elephants but alters temporal scaling for other species.
records.limits: Separate population/species and time unit; not human psychiatric/natal personality test.

records.locator: Lesson19 Sutra1.1.35 and commentary, PDF p391
records.source_paraphrase: The tiny printed sutra refers the study of Horā to established śāstra; Rath's expansive commentary lists Ashtakavarga, special aspects, charts and transits as contents of the tradition.
records.limits: The commentator's list is not explicit scope in the original single-line sutra; do not treat it as proof of original Jaimini authorship of every technique.

records.locator: Section74 Sudarshana Chakra, CP1252 lines5406–5412
records.source_paraphrase: This Portuguese transmitted Parashara section instructs three concentric twelve-house rings based on natal ascendant, Moon and Sun reference signs, rather than just ascendant houses.
records.limits: Extra combination method, not three independent predictions. Different longitude conventions and aspect rules need collation.

records.locator: Section74 Sudarshana Chakra, CP1252 line5426
records.source_paraphrase: If two or three among natal Ascendant, Sun and Moon occupy the same sign, the transmitted text restricts judgment to the ordinary natal chart rather than combining rings.
records.limits: Explicit suppression/override must be implemented; otherwise accidental triple-counting of matching sign.

records.locator: Section74 Sudarshana Chakra, CP1252 lines5428–5430
records.source_paraphrase: A cycle assigns one major year to each of twelve houses and a month subperiod to each house; conditional benefic/malefic placement modifies outcomes.
records.limits: Requires age/year start, date conventions and truly prospective scoring; no exact day precision assumed.

records.locator: Section74 Sudarshana Chakra, CP1252 line5432
records.source_paraphrase: The text compares yearly/monthly Sudarshana results to Aṣṭakavarga; if predictions agree effects are said to be full, if disagree compare their relative strengths.
records.limits: Source-derived corroboration is not independent empirical evidence; scoring must respect shared chart inputs and resolve disagreements before test.

records.locator: Efeitos dos Elementos, CP1252 lines5454–5456
records.source_paraphrase: Jupiter/Saturn/Mars/Venus/Mercury are assigned ether/air/fire/water/earth, with source claims about temperament conditional on relative strength; Sun/Moon singled out.
records.limits: Similar to Saravali Chapter38 dream/temperament descriptions and historical Ayurvedic types; possible common tradition, not independent science or medical facts.
